title: Source of Destiny
next_chapter_hook: A familiar voice echoed from the depths of the Source of Destiny—it was Chen Ji's own voice calling to him.

text.content:
Tianqing Sect Back Mountain Forbidden Grounds, the cold wind cut like a blade. Chen Ji stood alone at the cliff's edge, below his feet an abyss of endless depth, above dense clouds dark as ink churned. The Tianji Record Fragment in his palm radiated gentle warmth, golden patterns pulsing like blood vessels, as if responding to some ancient summons.

"From ancient times it came, sleeping at destiny's end..."

The voice rang out once more, no longer a vague echo in his mind but resonating truly throughout heaven and earth. The void tore apart, and from the rift emerged a towering figure like a mountain.

An elderly figure wielding a brush appeared, his entire form woven from countless flowing threads of cause and effect, each strand connecting to the fates of all living beings. His face remained indistinct, yet his eyes shone with perfect clarity—reflecting the entire cosmos yet seeming to transcend it.

"I am the Chronicler of Fate, the keeper of all causality through eternity." The elder's voice carried no emotion whatsoever. "Your possession of the Tianji Record proves you have touched destiny's edge. I have come to guide you—to the Source of Destiny."

dialogue.content: The Source of Destiny... what place is that?

text.content:
Chen Ji clasped his hands behind his back, his expression betraying nothing while storms raged within. The Tianji Record Fragment burned increasingly fierce, threatening to sear through his palm. Mo Xiansheng had once spoken that name—the source of Heavenly Will, the beginning and end of all cause and effect.

The Chronicler of Fate raised his brush, and a staircase materialized in the void leading into the abyss: "The deepest realm beyond heaven, transcending the cycle of rebirth. If you seek the complete truth of the Tianji Record, if you wish to break free from destiny's chains... there lies your only answer."

dialogue.content: "What is the price?" Chen Ji stared directly into those eyes that transcended heaven and earth, his voice cold. "Heaven's Will never engages in losing trades."

text.content:
The Chronicler of Fate fell silent for a moment, then brushed his brush's tip lightly. A sharp pain shot through Chen Ji's brow center—and he saw.

It was the true appearance of the Source of Destiny: a world-piercing divine tree, its roots delving into endless void, its canopy supporting billions of stars. Countless names were carved into the trunk, each one a being recorded by Heavenly Will. And deep within the trunk, a vague outline was slowly taking shape—the figure bore an exact resemblance to Chen Ji.

dialogue.content: "That is... me?" Chen Ji's pupils constricted sharply, his voice losing composure for the first time.

text.content:
"Past, present, future—to the Tree of Destiny, all are predetermined chapters." The Chronicler of Fate's voice finally carried a hint of波动. "The Tianji Record you possess, the struggle against fate you believe in... are merely scripts it wrote long ago."

Chen Ji's entire body went rigid. He thought of the Tianji Record's incompleteness, of the Heavenly Fate Value consumed with each use, of those seemingly coincidental yet precisely orchestrated arrangements—could all of this merely be the Tree of Destiny's arrangement?

The wind grew fiercer, whipping Chen Ji's robes.

He slowly closed his eyes, and when he opened them again, his gaze had returned to its usual depth and coldness. The youth who had struggled to survive in ruins, the servant disciple who had walked the world feigning mediocrity—his mind was now racing at incredible speed.

He bore grudges but never acted rashly. He committed this tree to memory, every word the Chronicler of Fate had spoken.

But now was not the time for settling accounts.

choice.prompt: The truth of the Source of Destiny was stunning, and Chen Ji had to make a choice—whether to pursue a cosmic truth that might overturn all understanding, or maintain caution?

choices.description: Whether ahead lay a trap or truth, Chen Ji chose to face destiny head-on. He wanted to see that divine tree with his own eyes, to confirm what that figure identical to himself truly was.
choices.visible_reward: Unlock Deep-Level Authority of Tianji Record

text.content: Chen Ji took one step forward, and the void around him twisted abruptly. The Chronicler of Fate swept his brush, and countless threads of cause and effect wound around him, enveloping his entire being.

As heaven and earth spun, Chen Ji felt himself falling into endless void. When he opened his eyes, the scene before him left him completely frozen—

A massive tree that could shroud the heavens stood before him, roots spreading into the abyss below, and on its canopy hung countless points of light—each one a star. And on the trunk, densely packed names squirmed slowly, like living ants.

choices.description: Chen Ji did not rush forward. Instead, he first used the Tianji Record Fragment's foresight ability to probe the dangers ahead. He knew too well the cunning of Heavenly Will, never willingly stepping into an unfamiliar game.

text.content: Chen Ji did not act immediately. Instead, he pressed the Tianji Record Fragment tightly to his brow center, golden light flooding his eyes. Scenes of the next three hours flickered past like a carousel—he saw himself entering the Source of Destiny only to be bound by countless threads of cause and effect, but also glimpsed another possibility: if he waited just another half hour, a variable would appear.

Chen Ji withdrew his gaze, a faint smile curling at the corner of his mouth: "Heavenly Will... Your chess game is indeed exquisite, but unfortunately, you've found the wrong opponent." He stood with hands clasped behind his back, leisurely awaiting the coming variable.

The eerie atmosphere of the Source of Destiny made Chen Ji hold his breath.

There was no wind, no distinction between light and darkness, no laws of the ordinary world. He floated in chaos, around him flowing star rivers and shattered time fragments. In the distance, the silhouette of the Divine Tree was faintly visible; with every step closer, he could feel some power beyond comprehension scrutinizing him.

That was the gaze of the Heavenly Eye—cold, examining, as if watching an ant attempting to shake the heavens.

"Interesting."

Chen Ji laughed softly, and that laugh echoed with strange rhythm through this ancient silent space. He recalled the rainy night he crawled out from the ruins, remembered the years he gritted his teeth and endured while being trampled underfoot, remembered the warmth that the Tianji Record Fragment brought each time he was at death's door—

He never believed in these so-called "arrangements of heaven."

Even if before him lay the source of destiny, even if that Divine Tree was carved with everyone's fate, he would personally tear apart this false script.

dialogue.content: "You say I'm a chess piece?" Chen Ji's voice was terrifyingly calm. "Then let me show you how a chess piece drags the chess player down from the altar."

text.content:
The Tianji Record Fragment suddenly erupted with dazzling golden light, countless ancient runes pouring from the pages and forming a brilliant cocoon of light around Chen Ji. This was Mo Xiansheng's hidden trump card—now awakened by some force, frantically absorbing the causal power within this space.

At the same time, a low rumble came from deep within the Destiny Tree. The silhouette identical to Chen Ji began to slowly turn its head.

choice.prompt: Chen Ji was about to grasp the truth of the Source of Destiny, but the silhouette identical to himself was awakening—how should he respond to this sudden change?

choices.description: Chen Ji decided to face destiny directly; he wanted that silhouette to personally tell him the truth. Whether it was his past life or a projection, he would get to the bottom of it.

text.content: Chen Ji walked through the void, moving directly toward the Divine Tree. With every step, the surrounding threads of causality wildly coiled around him, attempting to pin him in place. Agonizing pain shot through every limb and bone, as if countless needles were piercing his soul.

But he laughed.

This pain—what was it compared to that night years ago when someone broke his ribs and threw him into the mass grave? Gritting his teeth, step by step, he climbed onto the roots of the Divine Tree, walking toward the silhouette that was turning its head.

choices.description: Chen Ji did not act rashly; instead, using the foresight ability of the Tianji Record Fragment, he captured the silhouette's movement patterns, searching for weaknesses.

text.content: Chen Ji suppressed his inner impulse, expanding the Tianji Record Fragment's perception range to the extreme. He "saw"—that silhouette was not a true living being, but a sealed memory, a deliberately erased past.

More crucially, he saw the secret behind the silhouette: embedded in its chest was a torn page—that was another part of the Tianji Record! Mo Xiansheng's voice exploded in his mind: "Found it... the third page of the Tianji Record!"

The Destiny Tree shuddered, countless stars falling like rain.

Chen Ji stood atop the Divine Tree's roots, gazing up at the silhouette identical to himself. It had completely turned around, its features clearly visible—it was indeed him, yet not entirely him. Those eyes held none of his usual coldness and calculation, only a chilling emptiness.

As if... it was a body stripped of its soul.

"Welcome home."

The silhouette spoke, its voice identical to Chen Ji's yet carrying an echo that transcended time and space. At the same time, a voice so familiar it made Chen Ji's whole body stiffen came from deep within the Divine Tree—

"The Source of Destiny... indeed interesting."

That was Chen Ji's own voice.

But he was clearly standing right here. Where was that voice coming from?

Chen Ji turned sharply, only to see a crack split open deep within the Divine Tree, and another figure was slowly emerging from the fissure.

That was also a Chen Ji.

The same face, the same build, even the dust clinging to the robes was identical. The only difference was those eyes—deep, sharp, carrying a transcendental insight that saw through everything, as if a high-and-mighty deity gazing down at ants.

The true face of the Heavenly Eye... was now finally revealed before Chen Ji.

dialogue.content: "Surprised?" that Chen Ji—the Heavenly Eye—slightly lifted the corner of his mouth. "You think you're rebelling against destiny, but you don't know that this rebellion itself is also part of destiny."

text.content:
Chen Ji looked at this other self before him, and the last trace of hope in his heart completely vanished.

He finally understood why the Tianji Record Fragment would choose a waste of a boy from the ruins, why every scheme of his seemed dangerous on the surface yet terrifyingly precise—it wasn't luck, but a setup. From the very beginning, he was a chess piece arranged by the Heavenly Eye.

But so what?

Chen Ji slowly gripped the Tianji Record Fragment tighter, cold light suddenly flashing in his eyes. A chess piece also has the day it overturns the chessboard.

dialogue.content: "Is that so?" Chen Ji said softly, a dangerous arc curling at the corner of his lips. "Then let's make a bet—let's see if you, the Chess Player, laugh last, or if I, this Chess Piece... first shatter your chessboard into pieces."

text.content:
The Eye of Heavenly Way—that other Chen Ji—heard this and burst into laughter, the sound echoing through this ancient space, causing countless stars to tremble.

"Interesting... Most interesting!" A flash of appreciation flickered in its eyes. "The first creature in hundreds of millions of years to dare bet its life against me... Indeed, I did not choose wrong."

Before the words even faded, the Divine Tree suddenly erupted with blinding light, and countless threads of cause and effect surged toward Chen Ji like a tidal wave—this was the test of Heavenly Will, but also the opportunity it bestowed.

And in the instant before the light engulfed everything, Chen Ji heard a voice from the depths of the source of destiny. The voice was so familiar, so clear—it was his own voice—

"Chen Ji... find me..."
